title: UPI / bank account suspected compromise
summary: Money may move out via UPI if someone got your UPI PIN, app access, SIM/OTP, or tricked you into approving a collect request.
solution: 1) Immediately call your bank’s official customer care and ask to block/limit UPI & cards. 2) In your UPI app, check payee names and pending mandates; revoke unknown devices if the app allows. 3) Change UPI PIN only after you’re sure the device is safe. 4) File cyber complaint: call **1930** and report on **cybercrime.gov.in** with transaction details.
source_hint: NPCI dispute redressal for UPI issues; RBI guidance on reporting unauthorized transactions

title: QR Code / Barcode scam
summary: Scanning a QR code in UPI usually means you are paying, not receiving money.
solution: Always verify the merchant name in your UPI app before confirming. Prefer typing UPI ID or using official POS.
source_hint: NPCI UPI guidelines — verify payee before payment

title: UPI phishing / fake screenshots
summary: Fraudsters may show edited screenshots of successful payments.
solution: Verify payment only in your bank/UPI app or official SMS from the bank. Never trust screenshots alone.

title: SIM swap fraud
summary: Attackers may port your number to receive OTPs and drain accounts.
solution: Enable SIM lock with your operator, use app-based transaction alerts, and set low transaction limits.
source_hint: RBI customer awareness on digital fraud

title: Fake KYC / vishing calls
summary: Impersonators ask for OTP or card details pretending to be bank staff.
solution: Banks do not ask for OTPs or full card details on phone calls. Hang up and call the official bank number.
source_hint: RBI — banks never ask for OTP/password on calls

title: Fake / predatory loan apps
summary: Unregulated apps may charge extreme interest and misuse personal data.
solution: Check if the lender is RBI-registered before borrowing. Prefer known banks/NBFCs.

title: Investment / Ponzi schemes
summary: Unregistered advisors may promise unrealistic guaranteed returns.
solution: Verify SEBI registration of intermediaries and read official SEBI investor alerts.
source_hint: SEBI — check intermediary registration at sebi.gov.in

title: Insurance fraud / fake agents
summary: Fraudsters may sell fake policies or misuse agent identity.
solution: Verify agent license and insurer details on IRDAI/Bima Bharosa before paying premium.
